title: I found the pictorial instructions easy to follow
text:
I found the pictorial instructions easy to follow. It took me 40 minutes in total to unpack the bookcase and put it together. There are 9 pieces for the bookcase with 17 screws and 17 caps to cover the screw holes. One screw and one cap are left over as only 16 are needed. I found the pictorial instructions easy to follow. Note that there are two other tiny pieces of wood in the box which is part of the packaging material only. At first I thought it was some trim but it is not and that gets thrown out.

The package this arrived in was falling apart because it comes in a very small box and Amazon put it in a larger box causing the unit to slide around and push out the lid of the larger box. Other than this the boxes were not damaged.

The unit is made of particle board which is typical of cheap shelving like this. One of my shelf edges was damaged and it was not from the packaging (see first picture). When I did the installation, I made sure to flip the damaged shelf in such a way so that it is in the back of the unit (see the right side of the first shelf from the top in the second picture). The third picture shows the fully assembled shelf.

I only had to use a Phillips screwdriver for assembly and I used the top of the screwdriver handle to "hammer" in the screw caps because I was unable to seat them with my thumbs.

In summary, this is a cheap alternative for a bookcase and is not something that will last a lifetime of heavy use. It requires assembly. I have assembled a lot of my furniture over the past 30 years so I found it easy. However, I still had to review the specific instructions to determine which were the top and bottom panels and which way the divots should face. If I wanted a shelf that was longer lasting and looked more high-end, then this is not one I would buy. However, for a temporary solution or low budget needs, this works and is competitively priced for what it is
